units.translation: Where is the sacred speaking wood of Argos?
nor were there brick-woven houses facing the sun, nor woodworking.
the same as κοινός [common]. A word frequent in more elevated poetry and in Herodotus, foreign to the Attic dialect: see Thes. vol. 5 p. 1688.
Sophocles used it twice in dactylic and anapaestic verses, and Aeschylus twice in iambic trimeters, Sept. 76 ξυνὰ δ᾽ ἐλπίζω λέγειν [I hope to speak of common matters].
Let the people be concerned to work out remedies in common. Euripides never uses it.

ἐπὶ ξυροῦ [on a razor's edge] in extreme danger. Ch. 883 ἔοικε νῦν αὐτῆς ἐπὶ ξυροῦ πέλας αὐχὴν πεσεῖσθαι [it seems that now her neck is about to fall close to the razor's edge], a proverbial expression, on which see Thes. vol. 5 p. 1692.
